answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post an opal-grade stake before it may transact: a refundable bond locked for several epochs, slashed if the identity is caught attesting falsely. A zephyr of new accounts cannot overwhelm the network because each fake must fund its own bond, so creating ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand bonds while an honest agent pays once. An onyx ledger records every slash, making repeat offenders visible and permanently expensive to re-enter.
